name: Inox Center Ostalpen GmbH
summary: Inox Center Ostalpen is a privately owned Austrian stainless steel service center: 150 staff, 76.3 M EUR turnover, 34.2 % equity and a stable credit index of 167. It supplies our single 1.4301 sheet part at 100 % quota. It bought nickel and alloys forward until January 2027 and is quoting a flat 4.05 EUR on that basis, even though our framework contract has a quarterly index clause with no deadband. The framework runs to 2026-12-31 and auto-extends unless notice is given 60 days ahead. Its key account manager can move price by up to 2 %; anything larger goes to a pricing committee.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager up to 2 %. Above 2 %, the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks. The owner is personally involved and has offered to walk us through the cost calculation.

negotiation_pattern: Every annual renewal has ended below its own opening position, on average 2.3 pp lower. Asks were -6.4 %, +1.2 % and -0.8 %; settlements were -8.9 %, -1.2 % and -2.8 %. Mean settlement is -4.3 %. It even opened with an increase once and still settled on a decrease. It does not dig in. It negotiates through cost arguments: the material hedge ('market price not our reality'), and an offer by the owner to show hourly rates and material. Moves above 2 % are slower because they need committee approval.
wants: Recognition of its forward-bought material cost until January 2027 (no immediate pass-through of falling market prices)
A fact-based price settlement using its own calculation (open-book offer from the owner)
Continuity of the framework (auto-extension) and stable volume
Punctual payment at net 30 (low priority; it is not cash-short)
protects: unit_price until January 2027 (material hedged; quote held flat at 4.05)
Any price move above 2 % without pricing committee approval

trades.give: contract_months: extend 24 months instead of the automatic 12
trades.get: unit_price -2 % from 2027-01-01, within the key account manager's authority, plus the index clause unchanged (45 % material share, quarterly, 0 % deadband)
trades.why: A 2 % move needs no committee, and a longer contract secures the account for the supplier after its hedge expires.

trades.give: Accept the open-book walk-through offered by the owner; effective_date 2027-01-01 for any reduction beyond the index
trades.get: unit_price reduction on the 55 % non-material share (conversion and margin), justified by its own hourly-rate data
trades.why: Its hedge argument only covers material; conversion cost is open to discussion and the owner volunteered the data.

trades.give: payment_days: commit to paying punctually at net 30 (we are late on 84 % of invoices, mean 2.9 days)
trades.why: This is a cheap goodwill gesture from us that removes a weak point in our position, and it answers ppm nearly doubling.

trades.give: volume_per_year: a firm forecast or commitment for the 1.4301 sheet
trades.get: lead_time_days kept at 14 contractually and price held through 2027 except for index moves
trades.why: Gives the supplier planning security on a small, declining account.

arguments.point: The index clause is contractual: quarterly adjustment on 1 Oct and 1 Jan for any change above 0 %. Its forward purchasing is its own risk and does not override the formula. The 4.05 quote valid until January must be checked against the AS-14301 index for the 1 October adjustment.
Every past renewal ended in a reduction, average -4.3 %. A modest step from 2027 is consistent with the relationship.
We accept the owner's offer to review the calculation and want to settle on facts, especially hourly rates on the non-material 55 %.
Quality is still green but ppm rose from 46 to 89 within a year, with 6 complaints in the last 12 months. We want a ppm commitment in the renewal.
A second source exists for this standard material.

avoid: Threatening to pull volume as the main lever. We are only 0.3 % of its turnover and this will not frighten it.
Demanding more than 2 % and expecting a same-week answer. This needs the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks; plan for it.
Dismissing its hedge outright. Acknowledge it, then point to the contract formula.
Presenting ourselves as a reliable payer. We pay late 84 % of the time.
tone: Factual, respectful and partnership-oriented. Accept the owner's transparency offer and anchor firmly on the contract's index formula.
red_flags: Deadline: price-change notice and termination notice are both due 60 days before 2026-12-31, roughly 1 Nov 2026. If we miss it, the contract rolls over 12 months at the current terms.
The flat 4.05 quote 'valid until January 2027' may ignore the 1 Oct index adjustment owed under clause 3.2. Verify the AS-14301 move.
ppm has nearly doubled (46 to 89). It is still green, but the trend is worsening.
Our spend is declining (288 k to 278 k to 267 k EUR), which shrinks our weight further.

evidence.claim: Price changes above 2 % need pricing committee approval; the committee meets every two weeks.
Nickel and alloys are bought forward until January 2027; the supplier calls the market price 'not our reality'.
The owner offered to walk us through hourly rates and material.
Current price is 4.05, set by index adjustment on 2026-07-01; the latest quote holds 4.05 until January 2027.
Index clause: 45 % material share on AS-14301, quarterly adjustment, 0 % deadband.
Contract ends 2026-12-31 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice.
Financially stable: equity 34.2 %, credit index 167 unchanged; we are 0.3 % of its turnover.
Scorecard is green with A class, OTD 96 %, but ppm rose from 46 to 89.
Past renewals settled at -8.9 %, -1.2 % and -2.8 %, each below the supplier's opening ask.

indicators.credit_index: 167 (12 months ago 167; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 green (otd 95.8, ppm 46) → 2026Q1 green (otd 95.7, ppm 64) → 2026Q2 green (otd 100.0, ppm 90) → 2026Q3 green (otd 96.0, ppm 89)
